extrait-vs-eau-de-parfum.before:
Extrait de parfum, eau de parfum, eau de toilette: the words on the bottle tell you how concentrated the fragrance is. That affects how long it lasts, how far it travels and, often, the price. Here is what each label means and how to choose.

The labels, from strongest to lightest

Extrait de parfum (also "parfum")

The most concentrated form, typically around 20–40% perfume oil. Extraits sit close to the skin, develop slowly and can last from morning to evening. Italian house Tiziana Terenzi is known for them: Kaff Extrait de Parfum opens with bergamot, juniper and white iris before lavender, magnolia and leather settle into amber, musk and woods. Tiziana Terenzi Kirke, one of the house's most searched perfumes in the UK, is a fruity extrait, and Gold Rose Oudh brings rose and oud together.

Eau de parfum (EDP)

Usually around 15–20% perfume oil, and the most popular strength today. An EDP has good projection and wears for several hours. Good examples: Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition and Calvin Klein Eternity Eau de Parfum.

Eau de toilette (EDT)

Lighter, typically around 5–15%, with a bright opening that suits daytime and warm weather. Try Calvin Klein Eternity for Men Eau de Toilette or Davidoff Champion.

These ranges are typical, not fixed rules. Every house sets its own formula, which is why one brand's EDP can outlast another's extrait.

Same name, different strength

Many perfumes come in more than one concentration, and they don't always smell identical. Al Haramain's Amber Oud Gold Edition eau de parfum and the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait share the same fruity amber notes, but the extrait feels richer and closer to the skin. Calvin Klein's Eternity comes as an EDT, an EDP and a parfum miniature, which is an easy way to compare.

Which should you choose?

  • For all-day wear and evenings: an extrait, or an EDP layered over body butter.
  • For the office and everyday: an EDP, with one or two sprays.
  • For hot weather or the gym bag: an EDT, which you can reapply freely.
  • For gifting: an EDP is the safe choice; a travel-size mini lets someone try a new strength first.

Other words you might see on the label

  • Intense, Extreme or Elixir: a richer version of an existing scent. It is often closer to an extrait in feel, but there is no fixed rule, so check the notes.
  • Cologne or eau de cologne: the lightest style, usually fresh and citrusy, made for a quick lift.
  • ml: the bottle size. A 10 ml miniature is a low-cost way to test a scent on your own skin before buying 100 ml.

How to make any concentration last longer

Whatever the label says, skin matters. Fragrance tends to last longer on moisturised skin, so apply a little body lotion or butter to pulse points first, then spray. Keep bottles out of sunlight and heat, and avoid rubbing your wrists together. Our guide to layering oud with body butter walks through it step by step, and the body lotion for dry skin edit has easy bases to try.

Is extrait worth the price?

Per spray, often yes: you use less, and it lasts longer. But "stronger" doesn't mean "better". Choose the scent first and the concentration second. layer-oud-with-body-butter.before:
Oud is one of the richest notes in perfumery: smoky, resinous and warm. Yet even a great oud perfume can fade sooner than you expect on dry skin. The fix is simple and costs very little: layer it over a body butter. Here is why it works, how to do it, and three pairings from our shelves to try.

Why fragrance lasts longer on moisturised skin

Perfume oils evaporate fastest from dry skin. A thin layer of butter or lotion gives the fragrance something to cling to, so it tends to unfold more slowly and stay closer to you for longer. Rich butters with cocoa, shea or almond oil work especially well under warm notes such as oud, amber and vanilla. If your skin runs dry, a body butter for dry skin does two jobs at once.

How to layer, step by step

  1. Shower first. Pat skin almost dry; slightly damp skin takes butter more evenly.
  2. Warm a little butter between your palms and press it into pulse points: wrists, inner elbows, the base of the neck and behind the knees.
  3. Wait a minute so the butter settles.
  4. Spray once or twice from about 15 cm onto the same spots. Don't rub your wrists together; let it dry.
  5. Top up the butter, not the perfume, later in the day if skin feels dry. The scent often comes back with it.

Three skin + scent pairings to try

1. Sweet and golden: Chocolate Body Butter + Amber Oud Gold

The Deyga Chocolate Body Butter is made with cocoa and nourishing oils and has a light chocolate scent. Under Al Haramain Amber Oud Gold Edition, with its melon, pineapple, vanilla and musk, it reads as a soft gourmand. For more intensity, try the Amber Oud Extreme Gold Edition extrait. "Chocolate body butter" and "Al Haramain Amber Oud" are both popular UK searches, and this is the pairing that shows why.

2. Floral and warm: Rose & Geranium Body Butter + Amber Oud Ruby

The Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter carries rose and geranium essential oils. Layer it under Al Haramain Amber Oud Ruby Edition, which opens with saffron and bitter almond over jasmine, cedarwood, ambergris and musk, and the florals meet in the middle. If you love rose with oud, Montale Aoud Damascus is another lovely match.

3. Clean and smoky: a light lotion + Gucci Intense Oud

Not every pairing needs a scented base. A light, quick-absorbing lotion such as Vilvah Milk Body Lotion lets a dark scent like Gucci Intense Oud (black pepper, incense, woods, leather and an oud accord) lead the way, while still giving it something to hold on to. Want a luxury option? Try Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter.

Which base suits your skin?

If your skin is very dry, a rich butter such as Deyga's cocoa or rose formulas gives the most staying power. If you prefer something lighter in warm weather, a lotion like Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion absorbs faster and still helps the fragrance last. On sensitive days, keep the base unscented and let the perfume do the talking.

A few tips for oud

  • Less is more. Oud projects well; one or two sprays over butter usually lasts.
  • Spray clothes lightly, not silk, to keep a soft trail.
  • Match the mood. Sweet butters suit amber ouds, floral butters suit rose ouds, and neutral lotions suit smoky ouds.

how-to-use-body-scrub.before:
A body scrub is the quickest way to make skin feel smoother. It buffs away the dry, dull surface layer, so skin feels softer straight away and your body lotion or butter spreads more easily afterwards. But scrubs are not all the same: some are creamy, some are gritty, some are powders you mix yourself. Here is how to choose a body scrub, how to use it and how often.

What does a body scrub do?

A body scrub is a physical exfoliator: small grains, such as sugar, coffee or fine plant powders, gently lift away dead skin cells as you massage. The result is skin that feels smoother and looks more even and fresh. It also makes the next step work better, because a moisturiser goes onto clean, smooth skin rather than a dry, flaky layer.

Which type of body scrub is right for you?

Cream body polish: gentle and quick

A cream polish mixes fine grains into a soft, creamy base, so it cleans and exfoliates at the same time and can replace your shower gel on scrub days. Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish (£22.99, 200ml) combines coffee powder and ivory palm seed powder with shea butter, olive oil, argan oil and almond milk extract. It suits most skin types, including dry skin.

Powder scrubs: mix to the texture you like

Powder scrubs come dry; you mix a spoonful with water, rose water or toner into a paste. That makes them easy to adjust: a thicker paste for elbows and knees, a thinner one for softer skin. Deyga Body Scrub (£16.99, 100g) is a blend of dried fruit powders (lemon, papaya, pineapple, pomegranate and bitter orange) with purple rice. For something finer that also works on the face, Deyga Face & Body Exfoliator (£15.99, 50g) blends lemon, neem, matcha and black rice.

A luxury scrub in a jar

Highborn London Natural Luminosity Scrub (£50) is a natural exfoliant in a large 220ml glass jar, free from parabens and sulphates, in recyclable packaging. A good choice for a treat or a gift.

Tools: a loofah

Prefer to use your usual shower gel? A natural loofah such as the Deyga Organic Loofah (£12.99), made from plant fibres and biodegradable, adds gentle exfoliation to every wash.

Coffee body scrub: why it is so popular

A coffee body scrub is one of the most searched types in the UK. Ground coffee gives a satisfying, even texture and a warm, comforting smell that makes scrub day feel like a treat. Look for one in a creamy base with oils or butters, so skin does not feel tight afterwards; the Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish is a good example. Rinse the shower tray afterwards so grounds do not build up in the drain.

How to use a body scrub, step by step

  1. Warm up. Shower or bathe for a few minutes first, so skin is warm and damp.
  2. Take a small amount, about a tablespoon for each arm or leg.
  3. Massage in slow circles with light pressure. Let the grains do the work; you do not need to press hard.
  4. Spend a little longer on rough areas, such as elbows, knees and heels.
  5. Rinse well with warm, not hot, water and pat skin dry.
  6. Moisturise straight away, while skin is still slightly damp.

How often should you use a body scrub?

For most people, once or twice a week is plenty. Dry or sensitive skin may prefer once a week, or a gentler cream polish. Scrubbing every day can leave skin feeling tight or tender, so more is not better. Skip the scrub on skin that is sunburnt, irritated, broken or freshly shaved or waxed; many people scrub the day before hair removal instead.

Body scrub for dry skin: what to use afterwards

If your skin is dry, the step after the scrub matters most. A rich butter locks in moisture on freshly exfoliated skin:

  • Deyga Chocolate Body Butter (£15.99, 100g): cocoa powder, cocoa butter and shea butter with almond and jojoba oils, and a light chocolate scent.
  • Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99, 40g): shea butter, almond and jojoba oils with rose and geranium essential oils, in a handbag size.
  • Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter (£50), the partner to the Luminosity Scrub, in a 220ml glass jar.
  • Prefer something lighter? Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99) with oat milk, ceramides and olive squalane.

See all our body butters, and more ideas for dry skin.

Scrub sets

The Vilvah Body Polishing Kit (£48.99) pairs the Cookie N Cream Body Polish with a matching body mask made with kaolin clay, almond milk extract and coffee extract. The Highborn London Scrub and Glow Luminosity Set (£89) puts two Highborn products for face and body together in one box.

Don't forget feet and lips

Feet and lips need their own scrubs: body scrubs are too coarse for lips, and heels usually need a stronger one. For feet, use Deyga Foot Scrub (£17.99) once a week, then Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99) before socks. For lips, a sugar scrub such as Deyga Strawberry Lip Scrub (£10.99) or Vilvah Natural Lip Scrub (£6.99) is all you need; see all lip scrubs.

  • Patch test first on a small area, especially if your skin is sensitive.
  • Keep body scrubs off your face unless the pack says face and body: facial skin is thinner.
  • Keep water out of the jar and use dry hands to scoop, so the scrub stays fresh.

how-to-use-body-butter.before:
When skin feels tight and dry, a body butter is the richest way to put comfort back. It is thicker than a lotion, melts on contact with warm skin and leaves a soft, cushioned finish. Here is how a body butter differs from a body lotion, which one suits your skin, and how to use it so a little goes a long way.

Body butter vs body lotion: what is the difference?

The difference is mostly water. A body lotion is mainly water with some oils and butters, so it feels light, sinks in fast and suits everyday use. A body butter is made mostly or entirely of plant butters and oils, such as shea butter, cocoa butter and almond oil, so it is richer, takes a little longer to sink in and leaves skin feeling soft for longer. Body creams sit in between.

  • Choose a body butter for very dry or rough skin, for elbows, knees, shins and heels, at night, and in cold weather.
  • Choose a body lotion for a quick morning routine, for warm days, or if you dislike a rich finish.

Many people use both: a lotion in the morning and a butter at night.

Our body butters, compared

Chocolate body butter

Deyga Chocolate Body Butter (£15.99, 100g) is a short, simple blend: cocoa powder, shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil, cocoa butter and vitamin E, with no water in the ingredient list. The cocoa gives it a light, natural chocolate scent rather than a sweet perfume, which makes this chocolate body butter a favourite for evenings and a lovely small gift.

Rose and geranium body butter

Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99, 40g) swaps cocoa for floral essential oils: rose and geranium with shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil and vitamin E. The 40g size is small enough for a handbag, for dry hands and elbows on the go.

A luxury body butter

Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter (£50) comes in a large 220ml glass jar in recyclable packaging, free from parabens and sulphates. Its butter-soft formula is made to smooth over the whole body, and the brand says it can be used on the face too.

Body butter for dry skin: how to use it

  1. Apply after a shower or bath, while skin is still slightly damp. The butter seals in the water on your skin.
  2. Warm a small amount, about the size of a grape for each leg, between your palms until it softens.
  3. Press, then smooth it over the skin in long strokes, rather than rubbing hard.
  4. Add a little more to elbows, knees, shins and heels.
  5. Give it a few minutes to sink in before getting dressed. At night, it can work while you sleep.

Once or twice a week, use a scrub first, such as Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish (£22.99) or Deyga Body Scrub (£16.99). On freshly smoothed skin, a body butter spreads further and feels more even. Browse all body scrubs.

Prefer something lighter? Body lotions for dry skin

If a butter feels too rich, a body lotion for dry skin gives you the same ingredients in a lighter texture:

  • Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion (£14.99, 100ml): almond milk, cocoa butter, shea butter and almond oil with cucumber water. A good pick if you are looking for a cocoa butter body lotion that is quick to absorb.
  • Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99, 250ml): oat milk, ceramides, olive squalane, coconut and jojoba oils in a vegan formula, made for daily use.

See all body lotions for dry skin, or shop more for dry skin.

Feet and lips

Heels and lips are the driest places of all, and they have their own butters. Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) blends virgin coconut oil, olive oil, beeswax, vitamin E and vanilla essential oil; apply it at night and pull on cotton socks. For lips, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50) comes in a 15ml size, or a large 50ml.

Body butter and perfume

Perfume lasts longer on moisturised skin, because there is something for it to hold on to. Smooth an unscented or lightly scented butter over your pulse points before you spray. We explain how in how to layer oud with body butter.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with butters that contain essential oils, such as rose, geranium or vanilla.
  • Keep it cool. Natural butters soften in warm rooms and firm up in the cold; keep the jar out of direct sun and heat.
  • Not for broken or irritated skin. If your skin is very dry, cracked or itchy for a long time, speak to a pharmacist or your GP.

Deyga Rose & Geranium Body Butter (£15.99, 40g) swaps cocoa for floral essential oils: rose and geranium with shea butter, almond oil, jojoba oil and vitamin E. The 40g size is small enough for a handbag, for dry hands and elbows on the go.

A luxury body butter

Highborn London Natural Luminosity Body Butter (£50) comes in a large 220ml glass jar in recyclable packaging, free from parabens and sulphates. Its butter-soft formula is made to smooth over the whole body, and the brand says it can be used on the face too.

Body butter for dry skin: how to use it

  1. Apply after a shower or bath, while skin is still slightly damp. The butter seals in the water on your skin.
  2. Warm a small amount, about the size of a grape for each leg, between your palms until it softens.
  3. Press, then smooth it over the skin in long strokes, rather than rubbing hard.
  4. Add a little more to elbows, knees, shins and heels.
  5. Give it a few minutes to sink in before getting dressed. At night, it can work while you sleep.

Once or twice a week, use a scrub first, such as Vilvah Cookie N Cream Body Polish (£22.99) or Deyga Body Scrub (£16.99). On freshly smoothed skin, a body butter spreads further and feels more even. Browse all body scrubs.

Prefer something lighter? Body lotions for dry skin

If a butter feels too rich, a body lotion for dry skin gives you the same ingredients in a lighter texture:

  • Deyga Almond Milk Body Lotion (£14.99, 100ml): almond milk, cocoa butter, shea butter and almond oil with cucumber water. A good pick if you are looking for a cocoa butter body lotion that is quick to absorb.
  • Vilvah Milk Body Lotion (£25.99, 250ml): oat milk, ceramides, olive squalane, coconut and jojoba oils in a vegan formula, made for daily use.

See all body lotions for dry skin, or shop more for dry skin.

Feet and lips

Heels and lips are the driest places of all, and they have their own butters. Deyga Foot Butter (£12.99, 40g) blends virgin coconut oil, olive oil, beeswax, vitamin E and vanilla essential oil; apply it at night and pull on cotton socks. For lips, Highborn London Superior Lip Butter (£22.50) comes in a 15ml size, or a large 50ml. For the softest lips, use a scrub first: see how to use a lip scrub.

Body butter and perfume

Perfume lasts longer on moisturised skin, because there is something for it to hold on to. Smooth an unscented or lightly scented butter over your pulse points before you spray. We explain how in how to layer oud with body butter.

Good to know

  • Patch test first, especially with butters that contain essential oils, such as rose, geranium or vanilla.
  • Keep it cool. Natural butters soften in warm rooms and firm up in the cold; keep the jar out of direct sun and heat.
  • Not for broken or irritated skin. If your skin is very dry, cracked or itchy for a long time, speak to a pharmacist or your GP.
